---
title: Page Reference
---

The dashboard uses a **sidebar + main panel** layout. The sidebar contains the workflow navigation, a prerequisites checklist, and the **Execute Analysis** button. The main panel shows the content for the currently active page.

## Sidebar

The sidebar is always visible. It contains:

- **Workflow navigation** — buttons for Data, Explore, Configuration, and Results
- **Prerequisites checklist** — shows which required inputs have been loaded and whether the analysis has been configured. The checklist updates live as you work through the workflow.
- **Execute Analysis** — runs the full analysis against all configured SAF scenarios. Becomes active once all required prerequisites are satisfied.

---

## Data

The Data page is where all inputs enter the analysis. There are two paths.

### Path A — Upload your own data

The **File Upload** accordion on the left has sections for each required input. Expand each section to upload the corresponding file:

1. **Case study boundary** — GeoJSON, Shapefile, or GeoPackage with census tract geometries
2. **Demographics** — CSV with `GEOID` and `population` columns
3. **Baseline exposure** — either a tract-level CSV *or* AERMOD `.ADO` files (see below)
4. **Mortality rate** — CSV with `GEOID` and `mortality_rate` columns
5. **Per-capita expenditure** *(optional)* — CSV enabling monetized benefit estimates

**AERMOD exposure path:** If you choose to upload `.ADO` files instead of a pre-processed CSV, expand the AERMOD sub-section. Upload one or more landing-phase files and/or takeoff-phase files. Assign a numeric weight to each file (defaults to equal weight within each phase). Provide the CRS string for the receptor grid (e.g., `EPSG:32610`). The dashboard will derive tract-level UFP concentrations automatically.

See [Input Requirements](05-inputs.qmd) for detailed format specifications and guidance on obtaining each dataset.

### Path B — Load an example case study

The **Example Case Study** panel on the right lets you load a complete bundled dataset with one click. Select a case study from the dropdown and click **Load Selected Case Study**. Available case studies:

| Case study | Description |
|---|---|
| ORD Synthetic | 1,719 synthetic tracts, Chicago O'Hare metro area |

*[Screenshot: Data page — upload accordion on the left, example loader on the right]*

## Explore

The Explore page provides a spatial and tabular preview of the loaded datasets before running the analysis.

Use the **variable dropdown** to select which input to display:

- `population` — total population per tract
- `pollutant_concentration` — baseline UFP (pt/cm³)
- `mortality_rate` — baseline annual mortality rate (deaths per person per year)
- Additional demographic covariates if present in your tract file

The **map** renders the selected variable as a choropleth across all loaded tracts. The **data table** below shows the first 100 rows.

Use this page to verify that:

- All tracts loaded correctly and cover the expected geography
- UFP exposure shows a plausible spatial gradient relative to the airport
- GEOIDs are consistent across datasets (mismatches appear as missing values)

*[Screenshot: Explore page — choropleth map with variable dropdown, data table below]*

---

## Configuration

The Configuration page has two panels.

### Health impact function

Select one or more concentration–response functions from the library dropdown. The currently selected function's parameters and a dose–response curve are shown to the right.

The default function is **Bouma et al. (2023)**, which specifies a hazard ratio of HR = 1.012 (95% CI: 1.010–1.015) per 2,723 pt/cm³ increase in UFP for natural-cause mortality in adults. See [Methodology](06-methodology.qmd) for background on this function.

Use the checkboxes to select which functions to include in the analysis run. All selected functions are evaluated for every SAF scenario.

*[Screenshot: Configuration page — function selector with dose-response curve]*

### SAF blend scenarios

Enter one or more SAF blend percentages (0–50%) in the scenario list and click **Add Scenario**. Each blend percentage maps to a UFP reduction percentage via a built-in quadratic polynomial:

```
Reduction (%) = −0.0152 × SAF% + 0.00009 × SAF%²
```

The plot shows this reduction curve with your configured scenarios marked. All scenarios are evaluated in a single analysis run, so results remain directly comparable.

*[Screenshot: Configuration page — scenario list and polynomial reduction curve with markers]*

---

## Results

The Results page appears after a successful analysis run. It presents outputs at three levels.

### Summary cards

One card per SAF scenario, showing:

- **Attributable mortality cases avoided** — mean estimate with lower and upper 95% confidence intervals
- **Monetized benefit** — shown if per-capita expenditure data were provided

*[Screenshot: Results — summary cards row]*

### Scenario comparison

A bar chart comparing cases avoided (and economic benefits, if available) across all scenarios. Confidence interval bars are displayed.

Select a specific scenario from the dropdown above the geographic section to drill into tract-level detail for that scenario.

*[Screenshot: Results — scenario comparison bar chart]*

### Geographic visualization

A tract-level choropleth map for the selected scenario. Use the **result variable** dropdown to switch between:

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `attributable_cases_mean` | Cases avoided per tract (mean) |
| `attributable_cases_lower/upper` | 95% confidence bounds |
| `attributable_fraction_mean` | Fraction of baseline mortality attributable to UFP |
| `delta_concentration` | UFP reduction (pt/cm³) under this scenario |
| `mortality_value_mean` | Economic value of mortality reduction (if economic data loaded) |

The **detailed results table** below the map shows all result columns for each tract in the selected scenario.

*[Screenshot: Results — map and detailed table]*

### Export

Two download options at the bottom of the page:

- **Summary CSV** — one row per scenario with population-level totals and confidence intervals
- **Tract-level CSV** — wide format, one row per tract per scenario, suitable for GIS joins and custom reporting
